chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Hajj, so he said, 'Perform Tamattu'.'

Then he said, 'When we stand before Allah, the Exalted, we say: O our Lord, we have held fast to Your Book; and the people say: This is our opinion; and Allah will do with us and with them what He wills.'

key_terms.أَخَذْنَا بِكِتَابِكَ: We held fast to Your Book, indicating strict adherence to the Quran as the primary source of guidance.
key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' Hajj, a form of pilgrimage where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in between.
key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ: Standing before Allah, implying a state of presence and accountability.
key_terms.رَأْيَنَا: Our opinion/reasoning, referring to the reliance of the general people on their own intellect or interpretations.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Tamattu' Hajj and how does the Imam contrast the Ahl al-Bayt's approach with that of the general people?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) not only prescribes the ritual of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* but also articulates a profound theological dichotomy between the Ahl al-Bayt and the general populace. While the latter rely on subjective reasoning (*ra'y*), the Imams demonstrate total submission to the Divine Book, yet affirm that Allah’s ultimate decree (*ma arada*) prevails over both adherence and deviation, highlighting the balance between human agency and divine will in Shia jurisprudence.
